The submitter reports that with the package in -proposed, flows are refreshed on upgrade. This is the regression from LP #1940043 that the SRU was meant to avoid, so verification has failed and a new upload is needed.

The 19.2.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.1 package in noble-proposed drops the 'auth_supported' option, which breaks libvirt RBD storage pools (and CloudStack, qemu-img and similar users). The SRU team wants the option restored in a re-spun upload. A .2 build exists only in a PPA, has not been uploaded to noble-proposed, and has not been re-verified there.

The bug carries block-proposed-noble. The SRU team was asked to keep the package in proposed until libvirt LP #2172324 is resolved, and the ceph/libvirt interaction is not yet handled (no libvirt fix released, no Breaks or conflict declared against older libvirt).

Release-ordering prerequisite: every change in 19.2.6 must also be in resolute and stonking, which needs 20.2.4 to be released first. Otherwise users upgrading to an unpatched 20.x hit the CephX key-handling authentication failures. The 20.2.4 upload was still sitting unapproved in resolute as of the last status.
The libvirt autopkgtest on arm64 reported a regression against the ceph upload. It is probably linked to the auth_supported removal, but no analysis or retest has been recorded.

Earlier verification (CI run, verification-done) was done against the .1 package, which has the libvirt regression. The re-spun package needs fresh verification, and the verification-done and verification-done-noble tags are stale. The verification-caracal-needed tag is also still present.

The kernel-related decisions and communication about the CephX CVE change (client compatibility and release notes) were still unresolved. The Impact section and the regression potential text do not mention these upgrade or compatibility risks.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

blockers.summary: The reviewer (athos) questioned the DEP3 headers. The jammy patch lists Ponnuvel as Author while its referenced upstream commit has a different author, and the Forwarded field is unnecessary. Ponnuvel explained the reasoning and offered to use the upstream developers' names, but no corrected debdiff has been posted.

The Noble debdiff is built on 19.2.3, while 19.2.6 is already in -proposed. It must be rebased and re-uploaded on top of 19.2.6 once that lands. The upstream fix (PR 70762) is only targeted for the unreleased 19.2.7, so the Noble patch is not yet in a released upstream version.

The Jammy 17.2.9 fix is a hand-adapted, minimal patch with no upstream counterpart, because Quincy is EOL upstream. That raises regression risk, such as deadlocks on the non-recursive jobs_lock or scrubs not being scheduled. The test plan only covers a stress run for roughly 15 minutes, and the original crash cannot be reliably reproduced.
